title: Group 2; Alkanes, fuels and cracking
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR06#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t4 term and clue written for the game; PT04#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR06#N.9, PT04#N.5, OR06#N.11, PT04#N.9, OR06#N.14, PT04#N.15, OR06#N.17.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Soot
items.clue: The solid C that can form when an alkane burns in limited oxygen.

items.label: Haemoglobin
items.clue: Binds CO more strongly than oxygen, so the blood carries less oxygen.

items.label: Second ionisation energy
items.clue: Quantity for the change M⁺(g) → M²⁺(g) + e⁻, which falls down Group 2.

items.label: Carbon monoxide
items.clue: Toxic gas with no smell, formed when an alkane burns in limited oxygen.

questions.stem: Tetradecane is cracked: C₁₄H₃₀ → C₁₀H₂₂ + 2X. What is X?
questions.explanation: Left over after C₁₀H₂₂: C₄H₈. Shared between two molecules: C₂H₄, ethene. One alkane plus alkenes is a typical cracking result.

questions.stem: Which equation shows the reaction of strontium with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sr forms Sr²⁺, so the hydroxide is Sr(OH)₂. Two water molecules supply two OH⁻ and release H₂.

questions.stem: Methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen. Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: In a very limited supply of oxygen the carbon is deposited as soot, while the hydrogen still forms water. 1 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: Dilute sodium hydroxide is added to separate solutions of magnesium chloride and barium chloride. Dilute sulfuric acid is then added to fresh samples of each. Which observations are expected?

options.text: MgCl₂: white precipitate with NaOH only. BaCl₂: white precipitate with H₂SO₄ only.
MgCl₂: white precipitate with H₂SO₄ only. BaCl₂: white precipitate with NaOH only.
Both solutions give a white precipitate with NaOH and with H₂SO₄.
MgCl₂: white precipitate with both reagents. BaCl₂: no precipitate with either.

questions.explanation: Mg(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble but MgSO₄ is soluble. Ba(OH)₂ is soluble but BaSO₄ is insoluble.

questions.stem: Which pollutant in car exhaust forms from the air rather than from the fuel?
questions.explanation: Air is mostly N₂ and O₂. At the high temperature inside an engine they combine: N₂ + O₂ → 2NO. The fuel contains no nitrogen.

questions.stem: Strontium reacts more vigorously than calcium with dilute hydrochloric acid. The sum of the first and second ionisation energies is 1735 kJ mol⁻¹ for calcium and 1614 kJ mol⁻¹ for strontium. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Strontium has a larger nuclear charge, so it attracts H⁺ ions from the acid more strongly.
Strontium's outer electrons are further out and more shielded, so less energy is needed to form Sr²⁺.
Strontium chloride is far more soluble than calcium chloride, so the metal surface stays clean.
Strontium atoms have more electrons, so each atom can give more electrons to the H⁺ ions.

questions.stem: A gas heater burns methane in a small room. The window is shut and the air vent is blocked. Why is this dangerous?

options.text: Methane burns completely, and the carbon dioxide that forms is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so CO forms, which cuts the oxygen that blood can carry.
Oxygen runs short, so unburned methane builds up, and methane is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so the hydrogen in methane escapes as poisonous hydrogen gas.

questions.explanation: Limited oxygen gives incomplete combustion. CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than O₂ does. It has no colour or smell.
